text:
- chief complaint: bilateral knee pain after moving boxes up and down basement stairs over the weekend, with the right knee more involved on exam.
- history of present illness: the patient has a history of kidney transplant for polycystic kidneys, hypothyroidism, and arthritis. Bilateral knee pain began after repetitive box-carrying, with prior knee problems. Acetaminophen and ice gave little relief, and pain disrupted sleep on Saturday night. Recent transplant follow-up was reported as stable, and immunosuppressants are being taken as prescribed.
- physical examination: afebrile with normal heart rate and blood pressure. Stable two-out-of-six systolic ejection murmur. Right knee shows edema, erythema, tenderness to palpation, and decreased range of motion; left knee normal. Right knee x-ray shows good bony alignment with no acute fracture. White blood cell count not elevated; kidney function good.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: bilateral knee pain, occasional right elbow pain, and sleep disruption. Denies fever, chills, myalgias, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, fatigue, weight gain, and headaches.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: tramadol (Ultram) 50 mg every six hours as needed for knee pain. Synthroid continued, dosage not specified.
- follow-up instructions: rest, with an autoimmune panel and thyroid panel ordered. Reassess over the next couple of weeks, with imaging and physical therapy referral if symptoms persist.
